items.title: Frank Capp interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: I think Herb Ellis said some of them just need to figure out what not to play now.

ctx.x: Well what’s happened, thanks to our education system, they have allowed, or have created jazz programs. When I was in school, you couldn’t even use the word jazz. That was a no-no. There was no jazz education at all. In my high school, all I got was a music appreciation class and we listened to classics. Nothing. Jazz was an illegitimate music as far as that era of thinking was concerned. But certainly we know better than that now and certainly because of the great educational program, there is all kinds of young…
Yeah. I think Herb Ellis said some of them just need to figure out what not to play now.
That’s right. Exactly, exactly. But music is, all music is great, except one.
